program: B.Tech. in Electronics and Communication Engineering

program_educational_objectives.description: Provide solid foundations in mathematical and engineering fundamentals to creatively solve problems in electronics and communication engineering.
Make graduates responsible and sensitive to social, environmental and economic issues, with a sense of ethics and professionalism.
Make graduates capable to work in groups, lead teams in system design, and communicate clearly and precisely.
Engage in lifelong learning of electronics and communication engineering to face challenges of the dynamic world.

programme_outcomes.title: Engineering knowledge
programme_outcomes.description: Apply knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals and specialization to complex engineering problems.

programme_outcomes.title: Problem analysis
programme_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate, research and analyze complex engineering problems using first principles.

programme_outcomes.title: Design/development
programme_outcomes.description: Design solutions for complex engineering problems meeting specified needs with consideration for health, safety and environment.

programme_outcomes.title: Investigation
programme_outcomes.description: Use research-based knowledge including design of experiments, data analysis and synthesis to provide valid conclusions.

programme_outcomes.title: Modern tool usage
programme_outcomes.description: Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering/IT tools.

programme_outcomes.title: Engineer and society
programme_outcomes.description: Apply contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues in engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Environment and sustainability
programme_outcomes.description: Understand the impact of engineering solutions in societal/environmental contexts and the need for sustainable development.

programme_outcomes.title: Ethics
programme_outcomes.description: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and norms of engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Individual and team work
programme_outcomes.description: Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader in diverse and multidisciplinary teams.

programme_outcomes.title: Communication
programme_outcomes.description: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with engineering community and society at large.

programme_outcomes.title: Project management
programme_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge of engineering and management principles and apply them to manage projects.

programme_outcomes.title: Life-long learning
programme_outcomes.description: Recognize the need and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the context of technological change.

programme_specific_outcomes.title: Product development
programme_specific_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate and analyze real life problems solvable using ECE techniques and develop innovative, reliable, economic and eco-friendly solutions.

programme_specific_outcomes.title: Research aptitude
programme_specific_outcomes.description: Research on current problems in semiconductor devices, signal processing, telecommunications and data science using scientific knowledge and state-of-the-art tools.

effort_notation.T: Tutorial – 50 min per unit (marked * = optional, can be replaced by self-study)
effort_notation.O: Outside class / self-study – 1 hour per unit

semester_plan.notes: Activity Points minimum 20 required by end of Semester 4.
Activity Points minimum 40 required by end of Semester 6.

courses.title: Project / Internship / Program Elective - 2
courses.note: Students choose one of: Project (0L/0P/0P, 9O), Internship (0L/0P/0P, 9O), or PE course (3L/0T/0P, 6O)

courses.title: Project / Internship / Program Electives 3&4
courses.note: Students choose one of: Project (0L/0T/0P, 18O), Internship Program (0L/0T/0P, 18O), or two PE courses (6L/0T/0P, 12O)

institute_core.title: Mathematics I
course_outcomes: CO1: Formulate engineering problems as ODEs and solve them.
CO2: Solve linear ODEs with constant coefficients.
CO3: Find limits, check continuity and differentiability of functions of two variables.
CO4: Test convergence of sequences and series.
CO5: Find Fourier series representing periodic functions.
topics: First order ODEs, existence and uniqueness, linear ODE, orthogonal trajectories
Second order ODEs with constant coefficients, Wronskian, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Euler-Cauchy equations
Applications of first and second order ODEs, systems of linear ODEs
Functions of several variables: limit, continuity, partial derivatives, gradient, Lagrange multipliers
Parametrised curves, arc length, curvature, torsion
Sequences, series, convergence tests, power series, Taylor series
Periodic functions, Fourier series, Fourier integrals, Fourier transforms
references: H. Anton et al., Calculus, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
G. B. Thomas et al., Thomas' Calculus, 12th Edn., Pearson, 2015
E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
Apostol, Calculus Vol 1, Wiley, 2014

institute_core.title: Mathematics II
course_outcomes: CO1: Find parametric representation of curves/surfaces and evaluate integrals over them.
CO2: Use Laplace transform to solve differential and integral equations.
CO3: Test consistency of linear equations and solve them.
CO4: Diagonalise symmetric matrices and find nature of quadratic forms.
topics: Vector fields, divergence, curl, scalar potential, line integrals, Green's theorem
Double/triple integrals, Jacobian, polar/cylindrical/spherical coordinates, mass, moments
Surface integrals, flux, Gauss' divergence theorem, Stokes' theorem
Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform, convolution, shifting theorems
Solution of differential and integral equations using Laplace transform
System of linear equations, Gauss elimination, LU decomposition, rank, eigenvalues, eigenvectors
Cayley-Hamilton theorem, diagonalisation, quadratic forms, canonical form
references: E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
H. Anton et al., Calculus, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
V. I. Arnold, Ordinary Differential Equations, Springer, 2006
P. Dyke, Introduction to Laplace Transforms and Fourier Series, Springer, 2014

institute_core.title: Mathematics III
course_outcomes: CO1: Introduce fundamentals of probability and random variables.
CO2: Identify distributions and transformations of random variables.
CO3: Apply concepts of correlation and stationarity in stochastic processes.
topics: Basics of probability, axioms, conditional probability, independence
Discrete and continuous random variables, CDF, expectation, variance, MGF
Special distributions: Binomial, Geometric, Poisson, Uniform, Gamma, Exponential, Normal
Markov and Chebyshev inequalities, law of large numbers, central limit theorem
Joint probability distributions, marginal/conditional distributions, covariance, correlation
Transformation of random variables, bivariate normal distribution
Random processes: mean, autocorrelation, cross-correlation, stationarity (SSS, WSS)
Power spectral density, Wiener-Khinchine theorem, ergodicity
references: S. M. Ross, Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Engineers, 5th Edn., Elsevier, 2014
R. A. Johnson, Miller & Freund's Probability and Statistics for Engineers, 8th Edn., PHI, 2011
V. Krishnan, Probability and Random Processes, Wiley, 2nd Edn., 2006

institute_core.title: Mathematics IV
course_outcomes: CO1: Characterise a linear system in terms of vectors, linear combinations and span.
CO2: Understand projection, orthogonality and linear transformations.
CO3: Understand convergence, continuity and differentiability of real valued functions.
CO4: Construct optimization problems for real world applications.
CO5: Understand existence and uniqueness of solutions for optimization problems.
topics: Vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, basis, inner product spaces, orthogonality
Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, projection, least squares, linear transformations, SVD
Real analysis: sequences, compact/connected sets, continuous mapping, differentiability
Chain rule, mean-value theorem, Taylor's theorem
Convex sets, linear programming, unconstrained optimization
Gradient descent, Newton's method, Lagrange multipliers, KKT conditions
references: Jerrold E. Marsden & Michael J. Hoffman, Elementary Classical Analysis, Macmillan, 1993
E. Kreyszig et al., Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
Edwin K. P. Chong & Stanislaw K. Zak, An Introduction to Optimization, 2nd Edn., Wiley, 2005

institute_core.title: Electricity and Magnetism
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply vector calculus to describe electric and magnetic fields.
CO2: Identify symmetry principles to compute E and B fields.
CO3: Formulate and solve problems involving time-dependent EM fields using Maxwell's equations.
CO4: Analyze propagation of EM waves in vacuum and dielectric media.
topics: Electrostatics: Coulomb's law, Gauss' law, potential, Poisson/Laplace equations, conductors, dielectrics
Magnetostatics: Biot-Savart law, Ampere's law, magnetic dipoles, magnetized materials
Time-varying fields: Faraday's law, Lenz's law, mutual/self-inductance, Maxwell's equations, Poynting's theorem
Electromagnetic waves: wave equation, plane waves, propagation in dielectric medium
references: D. J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 4th Edn., PHI Learning, 2012
E. Purcell & D. Morin, Electricity and Magnetism, 3rd Edn., Cambridge, 2013
R. P. Feynman et al., Feynman Lectures on Physics Vol. II, Pearson, 2012

institute_core.title: Biology for Engineers
course_outcomes: CO1: Explain evolutionary basis of life and structure-function of biomolecules.
CO2: Describe cellular composition, communication, and principles of genetics.
CO3: Apply biological principles to food, agriculture, and environmental sciences.
CO4: Apply engineering techniques to create medical devices, diagnostics and therapies.
topics: Origin of life, Darwinian evolution, biomolecules (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids), central dogma
Cell structure, bioenergetics, signal transduction, cell division, Mendelian genetics
Human organs: brain, eye, heart, lungs; brain-computer interfaces, pacemakers, ventilators, stem cells
Human diseases, biosensors, vaccines, genetic modification of crops, biodegradation, biofuels
references: Reece et al., Campbell Biology, Vol. 9, Pearson, 2014
S. ThyagaRajan et al., Biology for Engineers, McGraw Hill, 2013
Fox, S. I., Human Physiology, 13th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2011

institute_core.title: Professional Communication
course_outcomes: CO1: Distinguish the role and purpose of communication at the workplace and for academic purposes.
CO2: Decide strategies and modes for effective communication in a dynamic workplace.
CO3: Combine multiple approaches for successful and ethical information exchange.
CO4: Estimate best communication practices to assist productivity and congeniality.
topics: Listening, reading comprehension, introductions, feedback, public speaking
Vocabulary development, critical reading, text structures
Effective writing: note-making, paragraph writing, official letters, emails, abstract writing
Communication theory, verbal/nonverbal communication, group discussions, presentations, digital communication etiquette
references: N. Bhatnagar, Communicative English for Engineers and Professionals, Dorling Kindersley, 2010
B. A. Garner, HBR Guide to Better Business Writing, Harvard Business Review Press, 2012
S. Kumar, P. Lata, Communication Skills, Oxford University Press, 2015

institute_core.title: Professional Ethics
course_outcomes: CO1: Develop a clear understanding of human values.
CO2: Understand and follow ethical aspects of the engineering profession.
CO3: Align with IEEE Code of Ethics in professional activities.
CO4: Assimilate elements of Academic Integrity and Honour Codes.
topics: Human values: morals, integrity, work ethic, civic virtue, honesty, empathy, self-confidence
Ethics in professional context, ethical responsibilities to consumers, safety, IP, environment
IEEE code of ethics overview, responsible behavior, avoiding harassment and discrimination
Academic integrity: honesty, trust, plagiarism, honour codes
references: R. S. Naagarazan, Textbook on Professional Ethics and Human Values, 3rd Edn., New Age International, 2022
A. F. Bainbridge, Ethics for Engineers, CRC Press, 2021
IEEE Code of Ethics – https://www.ieee.org/about/corporate/governance/p7-8.html

programme_core.title: Introduction to Programming
course_outcomes: CO1: Illustrate use of algorithms to solve real-world problems.
CO2: Design and develop programs to implement algorithms.
CO3: Apply object-oriented programming concepts (inheritance, polymorphism).
CO4: Assess performance of programs for basic algorithms.
topics: Computational thinking, Python basics, data types, strings, tuples, lists, dictionaries
Control flow, functions, recursion, aliasing, mutability
Exception handling, concurrency and parallelism, synchronisation
OOP: classes, objects, constructors, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes
Searching and sorting algorithms, asymptotic complexity
references: M. Lutz, Learning Python, O'Reilly, 2013
J. V. Guttag, Introduction to Computation and Programming Using Python, MIT Press, 2016
D. Phillips, Python 3 Object-Oriented Programming, Packt, 2018

programme_core.title: Introduction to Electronics
course_outcomes: CO1: Outline the working of basic electronic components.
CO2: Analyze linear circuits using network theorems.
CO3: Evaluate steady state performance of electric circuits.
CO4: Examine simple circuits involving diode, BJT and op-amp.
topics: History of electronics, modern applications
Circuit elements: resistors, inductors, capacitors, independent/dependent sources
DC circuits: Kirchhoff's laws, mesh/nodal analysis
Network theorems: Thevenin, Norton, Superposition, Maximum power transfer, Millman's
Steady state AC analysis, impedance, phasors, power factor
Diodes: characteristics, rectifiers, wave shaping, voltage regulators
BJT: operating regions, current mirrors, switch and amplifier circuits
Op-amp: inverting/non-inverting amplifiers, voltage follower, integrator, differentiator
references: Paul Horowitz & Winfield Hill, The Art of Electronics, 3rd Edn., Cambridge, 2015
S. Sedra & K. C. Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, 7th Edn., Oxford, 2017
Anant Agarwal & Jeffrey H. Lang, Foundations of Analog and Digital Electronic Circuits, Elsevier, 2005

programme_core.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply Boolean Algebra in digital circuit design.
CO2: Illustrate building blocks of combinational and sequential circuits.
CO3: Design combinational and synchronous sequential circuits.
topics: Number systems, Boolean algebra, logic gates, Karnaugh map, Quine-McCluskey method
Combinational circuits: adders, subtractors, comparators, encoders, decoders, multiplexers
Sequential circuits: latches, flip-flops (RS, JK, D, T, Master-Slave), counters, shift registers
Design of combinational circuits, hazard-free realisation
Synchronous sequential circuit design: Mealy and Moore FSMs, state assignment, state reduction
references: M. Morris & M. Cietti, Digital Design with Verilog HDL, 5th Edn., Pearson, 2013
Roth Jr. et al., Fundamentals of Logic Design, 6th Edn., Cengage, 2020
Brown & Vranesic, Fundamentals of Digital Logic with Verilog Design, 3rd Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2014

programme_core.title: Practical Electronics
course_outcomes: CO1: Choose appropriate components for specific electronic functionality.
CO2: Use suitable equipment for analysing parameters in electronic circuits.
CO3: Design and assemble electronic circuits for various applications.
topics: Basic electronic components: resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors, ICs, LEDs, relay
Diode circuits: half-wave/full-wave rectifiers, clippers, clampers
Transistor as amplifier: biasing, gain, frequency response, power, impedance matching
Battery characteristics, charging/discharging, protection circuits
555 IC: internal structure, astable and monostable operation
lab_topics: Familiarisation of electronic components and equipment
Reverse engineering of existing electronic product
references: Paul Horowitz & Winfield Hill, The Art of Electronics, 3rd Edn., Cambridge, 2015
Data sheets of various electronic components

programme_core.title: Electric Circuits and Networks
course_outcomes: CO1: Evaluate transient and steady-state response of first and second order circuits.
CO2: Analyze electric circuits in s-domain and obtain frequency response.
CO3: Model two-port electric networks using two-port network parameters.
topics: Transients: initial conditions, natural/forced response, RC and RL circuit analysis, RLC circuits
s-Domain analysis: Laplace transform, nodal/mesh analysis, network functions, poles and zeros
Frequency response, Bode plots, filter characteristics, Q factor, resonance
Two-port networks: Z, Y, H, ABCD parameters, series/parallel/cascade interconnections
Symmetrical two-port networks, image impedance, characteristic impedance
references: K. S. Suresh Kumar, Electric Circuits and Networks, Pearson, 2015
M. E. Van Valkenburg, Network Analysis, 3rd Edn., Pearson, 2015
W. H. Hayt et al., Engineering Circuit Analysis, 9th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2020

programme_core.title: Semiconductor Devices
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply solid state physics laws to understand semiconductor material properties.
CO2: Analyze and model semiconductor junctions and heterojunctions.
CO3: Analyze and model MOS systems and MOSFETs.
CO4: Apply simulation tools for analyzing semiconductor devices.
topics: Quantum mechanics, Schrodinger equation, crystal structure, energy bands, E-K diagram
Semiconductors: carrier concentration, drift, diffusion, Hall effect, continuity equation
P-N junction: equilibrium, IV characteristics, junction capacitance, breakdown, Schottky diodes
MOS system: accumulation, depletion, inversion, threshold voltage, C-V characteristics
MOSFET: structure, DC characteristics, channel length modulation, short channel effects, small signal model
Simulation using SPICE/MATLAB/TCAD; hardware experiments on diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs
references: D. A. Neamen, Semiconductor Physics and Devices, 4th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2021
S. M. Sze, Physics of Semiconductor Devices, 3rd Edn., Wiley, 2008
C. C. Hu, Modern Semiconductor Devices for Integrated Circuits, Pearson, 2010

programme_core.title: Digital Systems Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Design and implement combinational and sequential circuits using ICs.
CO2: Design basic logic circuits using HDL and implement in programmable devices.
CO3: Demonstrate output using technical reports.
CO4: Develop ability to work in professional teams.
topics: Introduction to Verilog: modules, ports, wires, registers, behavioural and gate-level modelling
Logic synthesis, RTL synthesis, Xilinx FPGA architectures
Implementation: combinational circuits, arithmetic circuits, flip-flops, counters, sequence detectors
references: Roth Jr. et al., Fundamentals of Logic Design, 6th Edn., Cengage, 2020
S. Palnitkar, Verilog HDL, 2nd Edn., Prentice Hall, 2003

programme_core.title: Signals and Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand foundational concepts in signal theory and system theory.
CO2: Analyze the interaction between signals and systems.
CO3: Understand basic principles of signal sampling.
CO4: Analyze discrete-time signals and systems.
CO5: Understand discrete Fourier theory and do Fourier analysis.
topics: Continuous-time LTI systems, Laplace transform, impulse response, convolution, transfer function
Poles and zeros, stability, Fourier transform, frequency response, bandwidth, Fourier series
Sampling theorems (lowpass and bandpass), discrete-time sequences and systems
Linear difference equations, z-transform, stability of discrete-time systems
Discrete Fourier series, DTFT, DFT, properties of DFT matrix
references: B. P. Lathi, Linear Systems and Signals, Oxford University Press, 2004
Oppenheim, Willsky & Nawab, Signals and Systems, 2nd Edn., PHI/Pearson, 2011
M. Vetterli et al., Foundations of Signal Processing, Cambridge, 2015

programme_core.title: Analog Circuits
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyze and design single stage amplifier circuits using transistors.
CO2: Estimate frequency response of amplifiers using suitable transistor models.
CO3: Design single stage and two stage operational amplifiers.
CO4: Use feedback theory in the design of analog circuits.
topics: Amplifier types, bandwidth, two-port network models
Large signal and small signal MOSFET models, common source amplifier, current-mirror biasing, source follower
High frequency MOSFET model, frequency response, Miller effect, cascode amplifier
CMOS differential amplifiers, CMRR, instrumentation amplifier, slew rate, offset voltage
Two-stage op-amp, negative feedback, stability, phase margin, frequency compensation
Oscillators: RC phase shift, Wien bridge, PLL as negative feedback system
references: S. Sedra & K. C. Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, 7th Edn., Oxford, 2015
D. A. Neamen, Electronic Circuit Analysis and Design, 3rd Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2006
Razavi, Fundamentals of Microelectronics, Wiley India, 2009

programme_core.title: Computer Architecture and Processors
prerequisites: A first level course in Digital Circuits
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyse basic building blocks of a computer system and the role of CPU using 8086.
CO2: Develop assembly language programs for 8086 CPU.
CO3: Examine features of 8051 CPU and peripherals.
topics: Computer architecture basics, system bus, RISC vs CISC, history of microprocessors
8086 architecture: execution unit, registers, memory segmentation, addressing modes, ISA
8086 instruction set: data transfer, stack, arithmetic, logical, string instructions, interrupts
8086 hardware: pin diagram, memory/IO decoding, interrupt vector table, DMA
8051 microcontroller: architecture, memory, assembly programming using Keil, port programming
8051 internal peripherals: timers, serial communication, interrupts
references: Lyla B. Das, The x86 Microprocessors: 8086 to Pentium, 2nd Edn., Pearson, 2014
M. A. Mazidi et al., The 8051 Microcontroller and Embedded Systems, 2nd Edn., Pearson, 2008
J. L. Hennessy & D. A. Patterson, Computer Architecture, A Quantitative Approach, 5th Edn., Elsevier, 2012

programme_core.title: Engineering Electromagnetics
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyze propagation of EM waves through transmission lines.
CO2: Analyze propagation of plane waves and incidence at interfaces.
CO3: Analyze two-port devices using S-parameters.
CO4: Design and simulate matching networks and passive microwave components.
topics: Transmission lines: voltage/current equations, standing waves, Smith chart, impedance matching, microstrip
Plane waves: Maxwell's equations, polarization, skin depth, reflection/transmission at interfaces, Brewster's angle
Guided waves: rectangular/circular waveguides, TE/TM modes, cut-off wavelength, dominant mode
S-parameters for two-port networks
EM simulation tools: waveguides, matching networks, tees, couplers
references: R. K. Shevgaonkar, Electromagnetic Waves, McGraw Hill, 2016
W. H. Hayt et al., Engineering Electromagnetics, McGraw Hill, 8th Edn., 2020
D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, Wiley, 4th Edn., 2012

programme_core.title: Analog Circuits Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Design signal conditioning blocks.
CO2: Analyse circuits using suitable models and software simulations.
CO3: Characterise circuits and estimate effects of parasitic components.
CO4: Develop ability to prepare technical reports and oral presentation.
lab_topics: Op-amp voltage follower, non-inverting amplifier, gain, frequency response, integrator, differentiator
Extracting small signal model parameters of a transistor

programme_core.title: Foundations of Machine Learning
course_outcomes: CO1: Discuss the role of data in computing and learn data processing, feature extraction, and ML model training.
CO2: Apply linear algebra, probability, statistics and optimization to ML algorithms.
CO3: Create ML algorithms for regression and classification problems.
CO4: Implement ML algorithms using a high-level programming language.
topics: Linear algebra, probability, decision theory, Bayes decision rule, optimization algorithms
Gradient descent, stochastic/mini-batch gradient descent, momentum
Supervised learning design cycle: data exploration, model development, evaluation
Linear regression, logistic regression, classification, cross-validation, regularization
Decision trees, Naive Bayes, Perceptron, MLP, K-NN, MLE
Unsupervised learning: PCA, LDA, K-Means clustering
references: M. P. Deisenroth et al., Mathematics for Machine Learning, Cambridge, 2020
G. James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning, Springer, 2013
Lyla B. Das et al., Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, I.K. International, 2023

programme_core.title: Communication Engineering I
course_outcomes: CO1: Demonstrate knowledge of analysis of random processes and signals.
CO2: Analyze generation and reception of analog communication signals.
CO3: Evaluate analog communication systems in terms of performance, bandwidth and complexity.
CO4: Analyze digital communication system processing blocks.
CO5: Demonstrate knowledge of passband digital modulation schemes.
topics: Analog communication: AM, DSB/SC, SSB, VSB, FM, PM, methods of generation and demodulation
Noise in receivers, SNR, figure of merit for different modulation schemes
Digital baseband: PAM, TDM, quantization, PCM, DPCM, line coding, ISI, Nyquist criteria, pulse shaping
Signal space representation, matched filter, correlation receiver
Digital bandpass: ASK, PSK, FSK, QPSK, MSK, QAM, M-ary modulation, signal constellation
references: U. Madhow, Introduction to Communication Systems, Cambridge, 2014
R. E. Zeimer & W. H. Tranter, Principles of Communications, Wiley, 7th Edn., 2014
B. P. Lathi & Z. Ding, Modern Digital and Analog Communication Systems, Oxford, 5th Edn., 2019

programme_core.title: VLSI Design
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyse static and dynamic characteristics of digital CMOS circuits.
CO2: Design static and dynamic CMOS logic circuits for given requirements.
CO3: Demonstrate performance of CMOS logic circuits using CAD tools.
CO4: Design arithmetic circuits and memories using CMOS.
topics: VLSI design flow, MOS transistors, MOSFET capacitances, scaling, short channel effects
CMOS inverter: DC/transient analysis, area, power, noise margin, layout
Multiple input static CMOS logic, logical effort, sizing for minimum delay
Logic styles: Pseudo-NMOS, DCVSL, pass transistor, transmission gate
Dynamic CMOS: charge sharing, domino logic, np-CMOS, sequential circuits
Timing: synchronous timing, clock skew, jitter, clock distribution
Standard cells, arithmetic blocks: adders, multipliers, barrel shifters
6T SRAM and DRAM cell design
references: J. M. Rabaey et al., Digital Integrated Circuits, 2nd Edn., Pearson, 2016
N. H. E. Weste & D. M. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th Edn., Pearson, 2010
R. J. Baker, CMOS Circuit Design, Layout, and Simulation, 3rd Edn., Wiley-IEEE, 2019

programme_core.title: Microcontroller Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Build small electronic systems using 8051/MSP430.
CO2: Choose appropriate designs for managing constraints.
CO3: Demonstrate output using technical reports.
CO4: Develop ability to work in professional teams.
topics: Embedded C programming using Keil Microvision IDE, interfacing peripherals to 8051
MSP430: pin-out, memory map, clock generator, interrupts, interfacing peripherals
GPIO, timers, interrupts, analog signal interfacing, relay/display/motor driver interfacing
Designing complete embedded systems for specific applications

programme_core.title: Control Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Deduce system models using block diagrams/system matrices and estimate performance parameters.
CO2: Analyse stability using time domain and frequency domain methods.
CO3: Design controllers using time domain and frequency domain methods.
topics: Open-loop and closed-loop systems, transfer function, transient and steady state response
Mathematical modelling of electronic and electro-mechanical systems
Block diagram reduction, signal flow graph, Mason's rule, steady-state error
State space representation, eigenvalues, time domain solution
Stability: Routh-Hurwitz, root locus, Bode plots, gain margin, phase margin
Controller design: P, PI, PD, PID controllers, lag/lead compensators
State space design: pole placement, controllability, observability, case studies using MATLAB
references: N. S. Nise, Control Systems Engineering, 8th Edn., Wiley, 2019
K. Ogata, Modern Control Engineering, 5th Edn., Prentice Hall, 2010
F. Golnaraghi & B. C. Kuo, Automatic Control Systems, 9th Edn., Wiley, 2014

programme_core.title: Digital Signal Processing
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyze time/Fourier domain representations of signals and systems.
CO2: Design and simulate fast algorithms for digital LTI system implementation.
CO3: Design digital systems for practical applications.
CO4: Analyze architectures for efficient DSP system implementation.
topics: DFT, DTFT, DFT properties, approximation of Fourier transform
FFT: Radix-2 DIT and DIF, prime factor algorithms, inverse DFT using FFT
Overlap-save and overlap-add methods
FIR filters: impulse response, linear phase, window design, frequency sampling, minimax design
IIR filters: structures, direct/cascade/parallel/lattice forms
IIR design from analog filters: Butterworth, Chebyshev, bilinear transform, impulse invariant
Finite word length effects, limit cycles
Multirate signal processing: decimation, interpolation
references: J. G. Proakis & D. G. Manolakis, Digital Signal Processing, 4th Edn., Pearson, 2007
Oppenheim & Schafer, Digital Signal Processing, Pearson, 2015
S. K. Mitra, Digital Signal Processing: A Computer Based Approach, McGraw-Hill, 2013

programme_core.title: Communication Engineering II
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyze fundamental limits on error-free representation of information.
CO2: Analyze and design optimum digital communication receivers for AWGN channels.
CO3: Evaluate performance of baseband and passband digital systems in AWGN.
CO4: Analyze fundamental limits on information transmission over noisy channels.
CO5: Design channel encoders and decoders for error correction.
topics: Source coding: entropy, joint entropy, Huffman codes, Shannon's source coding theorem
Signal detection: AWGN channel, MAP/ML detection, optimal correlation receiver, probability of error
Performance analysis: coherent/noncoherent binary and M-ary modulation schemes
Channel capacity: Shannon-Hartley theorem, bandwidth-energy trade-off
Channel coding: linear block codes, Hamming code, cyclic codes, convolutional codes, Viterbi decoding
Belief propagation decoding, capacity-achieving codes
references: T. M. Cover & J. A. Thomas, Elements of Information Theory, Wiley, 2nd Edn., 2013
J. G. Proakis & M. Salehi, Communication System Engineering, Pearson, 2nd Edn., 2001
S. Lin & D. J. Costello Jr., Error Control Coding, 2nd Edn., Pearson, 2010

programme_core.title: Communication Engineering Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Design, implement, test and measure performance of modulation/demodulation systems.
CO2: Compare theoretical and measured performance of communication systems.
CO3: Use tools to implement and evaluate communication systems.
CO4: Work independently and in teams to achieve targeted goals.
CO5: Demonstrate skills in oral presentations and technical report writing.
lab_topics: AM generation and envelope detection with AGC
Microstrip patch antenna design for wireless communication
BER evaluation for BPSK, QPSK, BFSK
Linear block codes and cyclic codes: encoder and decoder
Convolutional encoder and Viterbi decoder over AWGN

programme_core.title: Wireless Communication
course_outcomes: CO1: Examine multiple access techniques and network dimensioning.
CO2: Analyze effects of large-scale mobile radio propagation.
CO3: Differentiate wireless channel types and their parameters.
CO4: Analyze effects of small-scale mobile radio propagation.
CO5: Evaluate diversity techniques for communication with fading.
CO6: Analyze wireless techniques for wideband channels.
topics: Cellular concept: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA, frequency reuse, co-channel interference, cell splitting
Mobile radio propagation: free space, path loss, multipath, delay spread, Doppler spread, coherence bandwidth
Diversity techniques: selective combining, maximal ratio combining, beamforming, Alamouti scheme
OFDM: cyclic prefix, PAPR, OFDMA, single carrier FDMA, LTE/5G case study
lab_topics: Verification of theoretical performance of diversity
Implementation of OFDM generation and detection
references: T. S. Rappaport, Wireless Communications, Principles and Practice, 2nd Edn., Pearson, 2010
D. Tse & P. Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication, Cambridge, 2005
A. Goldsmith, Wireless Communications, Cambridge, 2005

programme_core.title: Computer Networks
prerequisites: A first level course in Programming
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe building blocks of a computer network and the Internet architecture.
CO2: Analyze network protocols and algorithms.
CO3: Evaluate and optimize performance of various network protocols.
CO4: Modify existing network technologies for resource efficiency.
topics: OSI and Internet architecture, layering, multiplexing, circuit/packet switching
Data link: framing, error detection, Ethernet (802.3), wireless LAN (802.11), LAN switches
Network layer: IPv4, addressing, ARP, subnetting, CIDR
Transport layer: UDP, TCP (segment format, connection management, congestion control)
QoS: queuing disciplines, weighted fair queuing
